items.title: Willie Hightower Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: And Roy got the band together. We got a fellow by the name of Pep Wallace on bass, Roy Palmer on trombone, myself on conant

ctx.x: And he laughed. He says, no. He says, Joe Oliver is all right. Freddie Kepler's all right. He said, but you want to learn music. Oh, I said, I'll learn all right. He said, but you better watch yourself. And he couldn't talk and he went on down the street. Well, every evening he'd pass by there going home, not late at night, but it'd be in the early part of the night. I'd see him maybe three or four times a week. So Roy knew music. But Roy never coaxed me with the music end of it. Roy, to teach me how to play,…

items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: Because most of the work that he got was two long grounds that we worked at up there.

ctx.x: So maybe he moved down to your neighborhood? No, never did he.

He stayed up in that part of the country, up in that part of the city. Because most of the work that he got was two long grounds that we worked at up there. That's the one that helped us a lot. He knew the people up there, see? And after we got straightened out and, as I told you, could play, that's where we made our greatest reputation up there. Because then most of the time, I hadn't come down to the district where I met Wade Whaley and we had to sign it. We was using Bechet up there, there, see? Oh, yeah. And…
One more question about the, did you ever play any parades very much in New Orleans?

items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: I think he played with you with Hightower's band

ctx.x: go ahead now and try not to make too many mistakes.

Because he was listening. They're teachers. This man was teaching these young fellas, and they had a big band. And he was telling them, I could see him telling them something. I don't know what he was telling them. He was telling them something. And they stood there, and those guys stayed right around me. I kind of felt embarrassed, you know. But they never heard the trombone thing. That was the trombone they ever heard. So that was one of my attempts to find out whether I was good or not. And after we come back…
